variants.name: Meadow
variants.atmosphere: A radius-three grassy clearing surrounds the shrine, edged with a continuous bush rim. Outside, bushes occupy 15% of cells; no grass or ordinary flowers. Three wild roses remain as special finds.

variants.name: Mushroom Grove
variants.atmosphere: Staggered mushroom pairs repeat every six cells, with giant woody mushrooms between them. The close-set caps lead to a crescent and its luminous flower.

variants.name: Orchard
variants.atmosphere: Regular apple rows alternate with medium maple rows, with open aisles leading to three finite gemfruit finds.

variants.name: Formal Garden
variants.atmosphere: Compact square flower beds step along short straight shrub rows; blue forget-me-nots dominate, with occasional whole orange beds.

variants.name: Hedge Garden
variants.atmosphere: Sixteen garden rooms form a clear 4 × 4 square. The POI is centered in an inner room, framed by four marigolds. Two roses distinguish the far corner rooms. A stationary carnivorous plant replaces one hedge seat in each repeated garden plot.

variants.name: Ancient Grove
variants.atmosphere: Rounded clusters centered on the largest mature deciduous trees repeat six cells apart, surrounded by bushes and grass. A light scatter of grass crosses the gaps; stone markers lead from the central grove to its guarded starflower. One stationary carnivorous plant replaces a bush beside each repeated central tree.

variants.name: Stone Garden
variants.atmosphere: Three concentric stone rings surround the POI, with softer grass rings between. Every fifth stone is iron, creating a regular metallic rhythm through the circles.

variants.name: Ordered Graves
variants.atmosphere: Short grave rows leave an aisle; matching finds occupy two empty row ends.

variants.name: Overgrown Graves
variants.atmosphere: Vegetation follows the old rows; a deliberate gap opens onto a lone flower.

variants.name: Broken Masonry
variants.atmosphere: Repeated piles suggest fallen walls; one displaced line ends at a platinum-bearing rock guarded by a club goblin.

variants.name: Silent Circle
variants.atmosphere: Touching stone circles form a continuous quiet lattice, with one off-axis grass entrance per circle and a single starflower find.

variants.name: Flint Field
variants.atmosphere: A radius-two flint circle surrounds the POI, edged with a continuous rubble rim. Rubble scatters at 15% outside; three gemfruit finds remain.

variants.name: Broken Depot
variants.atmosphere: Repeated rubble piles are threaded with traps. An offset line leads toward two finds; the broken order suggests an ambush.

variants.name: Seep
variants.atmosphere: Repeated tar-pit clusters seep around small rubble islands. A lone flower survives beyond the last dark crescent.

variants.name: Work Yard
variants.atmosphere: Copper-rock rows and rubble columns enclose twenty-five plots. The POI sits in the central room; a crimson-bearing rock marks the far end of its lane.

variants.name: Black Ring
variants.atmosphere: Smaller, near-continuous rubble circles enclose tight tar rings. The circles repeat every eight cells; two gold-bearing rocks stand at the far side.

variants.name: Mystic Reef
variants.atmosphere: Compact stone crescents, shell inlays and a blue flower center repeat every 6 × 6 cells. The single starflower remains the rare luminous find.

variants.name: Pirate Cove
variants.atmosphere: Driftwood ribs and shell fragments surround one shipwreck shrine, with a reserved 3 × 3-cell footprint and one daily gift. A pirate grunt and gunner hold the separate gold-ore find. If the full wreck cannot fit on dry sand, the accessible small shrine remains.

variants.name: Shellwater Strand
variants.atmosphere: Short shell ribbons and one driftwood seat repeat in a narrow 3 × 5 frame. Open sand separates them; the two wild roses stay on eligible landward vegetation.
